props.title: Breathless
props.initialSlug: Live Fast. Love Hard. Die Young.

sections.content: Breathless revolutionized cinema by breaking every rule in the filmmaking handbook. Jean-Luc Godard's debut feature smashed conventional editing with jump cuts, ignored traditional story structure, and turned Jean-Paul Belmondo into the epitome of French New Wave cool. The film follows small-time crook Michel as he kills a cop and hides out with American student Patricia, but plot was never Godard's primary concern. Like The 400 Blows (1959) and Cléo from 5 to 7 (1962), Breathless captured the rebellious spirit of young French filmmakers who were determined to make movies their own way.

movies.title: Breathless
movies.slug: A small-time thief kills a policeman and hides out with his American girlfriend in Paris while planning an escape to Italy. Defined the French New Wave with its innovative editing and cool detachment.

movies.title: Pierrot le Fou
movies.slug: A married man abandons his family to pursue adventure with his ex-girlfriend, leading to a crime spree across France. Features Godard's signature blend of pop art and politics.

sections.content: The influence of Breathless on modern cinema cannot be overstated. Directors like Quentin Tarantino with Pulp Fiction (1994) and Wong Kar-wai with Chungking Express (1994) directly borrowed from Godard's playbook of fragmented narratives and style-as-substance filmmaking. The film's documentary-like street scenes, shot with handheld cameras by cinematographer Raoul Coutard, inspired the cinema vérité movement and influenced directors like Martin Scorsese in Mean Streets (1973).

Beyond technical innovation, Breathless created a new kind of movie hero. Belmondo's Michel, with his Humphrey Bogart obsession and existential cool, became the prototype for countless movie antiheroes. This DNA can be seen in characters from Drive (2011) to Inside Llewyn Davis (2013) - protagonists who maintain their detached cool even as their worlds crumble around them. SUBHEAD: The Legacy of the French New Wave

movies.title: À bout de souffle
movies.slug: American remake of Breathless starring Richard Gere, updating the story to contemporary Los Angeles while maintaining the original's style.

sections.content: The French New Wave that Breathless helped launch transformed global cinema. Fellow pioneers like François Truffaut with Jules and Jim (1962) and Agnes Varda with La Pointe Courte (1955) shared Godard's desire to break from tradition. Their collective influence spread to New Hollywood with films like Bonnie and Clyde (1967) and The Graduate (1967), which adopted the movement's naturalistic acting and location shooting. The DNA of Breathless can even be found in modern independent films like Frances Ha (2012) and Cold War (2018).
